purpose: Levalbuterol is a rescue inhaler used to quickly relieve or prevent bronchospasm, which is the sudden tightening of the airways that makes it hard to breathe. It is commonly used for people with asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It works fast to open up your airways so you can breathe more easily.
how_it_works: When you inhale this medicine, it attaches to special receptors in the muscles surrounding your airways. This causes those muscles to relax and loosen up, which opens your airways wider. Think of it like loosening a tight belt around your lungs so air can flow in and out more freely.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include a faster heartbeat, feeling shaky or jittery, headache, dizziness, and a nervous or anxious feeling. Some people also notice a dry or irritated throat or a mild cough. These effects are usually short-lived and go away on their own.
warnings: If your rescue inhaler does not seem to be helping or you need to use it more often than usual, contact your doctor right away — this could mean your condition is getting worse. Do not use more than prescribed, as overuse can cause serious heart problems. Tell your doctor if you have a heart condition, high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid problems, as this medicine may affect those conditions.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 4 years and older, the usual dose is 1 to 2 puffs from the inhaler every 4 to 6 hours as needed. For preventing exercise-induced breathing problems, use 2 puffs about 15 to 30 minutes before exercise. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing can vary based on your age and condition.
